title: Cross-Framework Governance Indicator Mining: Building a Unified AI Safety Indicator Corpus

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: a unified corpus is a public good that enables downstream research, but the corpus itself does not produce safety-relevant findings. Impact depends entirely on uptake.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: NLP-based extraction and normalization is well within CS student capabilities. Parsing governance documents and deduplicating entries is a tractable data engineering project.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: parsing 10-15 frameworks, extracting indicators, normalizing, and deduplicating is substantial work. The scope is bounded by framework count but each framework requires careful reading.

novelty.reasoning: The FLI AI Safety Index (2024, Winter 2025, Summer 2025) already defines a comprehensive indicator set across governance domains. The International AI Safety Report (2025, 2026) and the G7 Hiroshima AI Process Reporting Framework provide cross-framework governance indicators. However, no existing work uses NLP-based automated extraction to build a unified, deduplicated indicator corpus from raw governance documents. The data engineering angle (NLP extraction + normalization + dedup) is novel, though the governance indicator landscape itself is well-mapped manually.

evidence: FLI AI Safety Index (2024, Winter 2025, Summer 2025). Future of Life Institute.
